samuel1.20.p1.b1.text: What have I done? What is my iniquity? How have I sinned against your father, that he wants to take my life?

samuel1.20.p1.b2.text: Far from it! … You will not die …

samuel1.20.p1.b3.text: … As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.

samuel1.20.p1.b4.text: Whatever you desire, I will do for you.

samuel1.20.p2.b1.text: Look, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I am supposed to dine with the king. Instead, let me go and hide in the field until the third evening from now.

samuel1.20.p2.b2.text: … If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?

samuel1.20.p2.b3.text: Never! … If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?

samuel1.20.p2.b4.text: “Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.” So the two of them went out into the field,

samuel1.20.p3.b1.text: By the LORD, the God of Israel …

samuel1.20.p3.b2.text: … May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.

samuel1.20.p3.b3.text: and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household—not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”

samuel1.20.p3.b4.text: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.

samuel1.20.p4.b1.text: When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.

samuel1.20.p4.b2.text: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.

samuel1.20.p4.b3.text: But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.

samuel1.20.p4.b4.text: And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”

samuel1.20.p5.b1.text: So David hid in the field,

samuel1.20.p5.b2.text: and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.

samuel1.20.p5.b3.text: He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.

samuel1.20.p5.b4.text: … Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.

samuel1.20.p6.b1.text: But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty,

samuel1.20.p6.b2.text: Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?

samuel1.20.p6.b3.text: David urgently requested my permission to go to Bethlehem …

samuel1.20.p6.b4.text: That is why he did not come to the king’s table.

samuel1.20.p7.b1.text: You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame …

samuel1.20.p7.b2.text: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingship shall be established. … he must surely die!

samuel1.20.p7.b3.text: Why must he be put to death? … What has he done?

samuel1.20.p8.b1.text: Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him; so Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.

samuel1.20.p8.b2.text: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger and did not eat any food that second day of the month, for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.

samuel1.20.p9.b1.text: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.

samuel1.20.p9.b2.text: Run and find the arrows I shoot.

samuel1.20.p9.b4.text: Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!

samuel1.20.p10.b1.text: But the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.

samuel1.20.p10.b2.text: Go, take it back to the city.

samuel1.20.p11.b1.text: When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times …

samuel1.20.p11.b2.text: Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together—though David wept more.

samuel1.20.p11.b3.text: Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’

samuel1.20.p11.b4.text: Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.
